test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 22 Aug 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A 210 m long train crosses a man walking at a speed of 4.5 km/h in the opposite direction in 12 seconds. What is the speed (in km/h) of the train?
solution:
**Given:**

Length of the train = 210m

Speed = 4.5 km/h 

Time = 12 sec

**Formula used:**

Distance = Speed × time

When two bodies move in opposite direction

Then their relative speed = Sum of speeds

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of the train be x km/h

Here, length of the train = 210m = 210/1000 = 0.21km [1km = 1000m]

Time = 12sec = 12/3600 = 1/300 hr [As, 1 hour = 3600sec]

Speed of man = 4.5 km/h 

As, they walk in opposite direction

Their relative speed = x + 4.5 

Now, distance = speed × time

⇒ 0.21 = ( x + 4.5) × 1/300 

⇒ 63 = x + 4.5 

⇒ x = 58.5 km/h

**Hence, the required speed is 58.5 km/h .**
